**Date:** 17/02/2026
**Technician:** TB
**Call Type:** Call-out – paper jam error E-202 recurring

**Reported by:** Margaret (office manager) – machine showing jam message on lower tray 2. Cleared by staff twice on 16/02 but jam returned within a few sheets.

**Diagnosis:**
- Removed tray 2 fully. Found a small fragment of a paper label (approx. 15mm x 8mm) lodged in the feed roller assembly, just behind the separation pad. This was not visible from the tray; it had been pulled down between the roller and the pad.
- The fragment appeared to be from an adhesive address label. The backing paper had separated from the label itself, which is what caused the intermittent pickup issue.

**Work carried out:**
- Removed fragment.
- Cleaned feed rollers and separation pad with isopropyl alcohol.
- Ran 50-sheet test through tray 2 – no further jams.

**Parts replaced:** None.

**Recommendation to site:** Use only plain paper in trays 1 and 2. Labels should be run through the bypass tray (tray 5) with the label setting selected. This is the second occurrence of label-related jams on this machine (see entry 14/11/2024). Consider placing a note near the machine.

**Signed:** T. Brightwell

**Date:** 14/11/2024
**Technician:** TB
**Call Type:** Call-out – jam in fuser area, error E-305

The SharpCopy MFP-350 copier has serial number SC-MFP-2847 recorded in the purchase record. Record status: current.

**Reported by:** Claire (accounts) – machine stopped mid-run, error E-305. She had already removed two sheets of torn paper from the fuser exit.

**Diagnosis:**
- The jam was caused by a sheet of adhesive labels (A4, 21-per-sheet) that had been run from tray 1. The labels had peeled away from the backing sheet inside the fuser, leaving adhesive residue on the upper fuser roller.
- The residue was causing subsequent sheets to stick and wrap around the roller.

**Work carried out:**
- Removed the offending sheet and a further three sheets that had backed up.
- Cleaned the fuser roller with the manufacturer-approved cleaner (part no. SC-CLN-200) and allowed a 20-minute cool-down before a test run.
- Ran 20 sheets of plain paper – clean output, no marks.

**Parts replaced:** None. Cleaner used from stock.

**Recommendation:** Labels must not be run from trays 1 or 2. Use bypass tray only. This was discussed with staff at the time.

**Date:** 17/02/2026
**Technician:** TB
**Call Type:** Call-out – paper jam error E-202 recurring

**Reported by:** Margaret (office manager) – machine showing jam message on lower tray 2. Cleared by staff twice on 16/02 but jam returned within a few sheets.

**Diagnosis:**
- Removed tray 2 fully. Found a small fragment of a paper label (approx. 15mm x 8mm) lodged in the feed roller assembly, just behind the separation pad. This was not visible from the tray; it had been pulled down between the roller and the pad.
- The fragment appeared to be from an adhesive address label. The backing paper had separated from the label itself, which is what caused the intermittent pickup issue.

**Work carried out:**
- Removed fragment.
- Cleaned feed rollers and separation pad with isopropyl alcohol.
- Ran 50-sheet test through tray 2 – no further jams.

**Parts replaced:** None.

**Recommendation to site:** Use only plain paper in trays 1 and 2. Labels should be run through the bypass tray (tray 5) with the label setting selected. This is the second occurrence of label-related jams on this machine (see entry 14/11/2024). Consider placing a note near the machine.

**Signed:** T. Brightwell

---

**Date:** 14/11/2024
**Technician:** TB
**Call Type:** Call-out – jam in fuser area, error E-305

The SharpCopy MFP-350 copier has serial number SC-MFP-2847 recorded in the purchase record. Record status: current.

**Reported by:** Claire (accounts) – machine stopped mid-run, error E-305. She had already removed two sheets of torn paper from the fuser exit.

**Diagnosis:**
- The jam was caused by a sheet of adhesive labels (A4, 21-per-sheet) that had been run from tray 1. The labels had peeled away from the backing sheet inside the fuser, leaving adhesive residue on the upper fuser roller.
- The residue was causing subsequent sheets to stick and wrap around the roller.

**Work carried out:**
- Removed the offending sheet and a further three sheets that had backed up.
- Cleaned the fuser roller with the manufacturer-approved cleaner (part no. SC-CLN-200) and allowed a 20-minute cool-down before a test run.
- Ran 20 sheets of plain paper – clean output, no marks.

**Parts replaced:** None. Cleaner used from stock.

**Recommendation:** Labels must not be run from trays 1 or 2. Use bypass tray only. This was discussed with staff at the time.

**Signed:** T. Brightwell

The supplier (Norfolk Office Supplies) has confirmed the part is on back order with an expected delivery of 17/03/2026.

The part is not critical at this stage. It will be fitted at the next scheduled service (01/06/2026) or earlier if a fault develops. If the machine starts showing vertical banding on colour prints before the part arrives, contact the supplier to expedite.

**Fault:** Colour copies showing faint horizontal lines across the page, mainly in the cyan and magenta areas. Problem started approximately a week ago and has gradually worsened.

**Diagnosis:**
- Ran a colour calibration test – output showed distinct banding in cyan and magenta.
- Inspected the transfer belt – found a small patch of toner build-up on the belt surface.
- Checked the transfer roller (SC-ROL-114) – noted slight wear but not yet at the point of causing faults. This was flagged for monitoring at the next service.

**Work carried out:**

- Ran calibration twice – banding cleared.
- Advised that the transfer roller will need replacing in the next 6–12 months depending on usage. This was noted for the maintenance schedule.

**Recommendation:** Monitor colour output over the next few weeks. If banding returns, the transfer roller should be replaced sooner rather than later.
